Jahaz
JAY-haz
proper noun
Hebrew Yahats, perhaps “a place trodden down” or “a battlefield,” a town in the plain east of Jordan.

Biblical Definition

Jahaz was a town on the tableland east of the Jordan, remembered chiefly as the place where Sihon king of the Amorites met Israel in battle and was overthrown. When Israel asked leave to pass peaceably through his land, Sihon would not suffer them, but gathered all his people and came out against them into the wilderness; he came to Jahaz and fought against Israel, and Israel smote him with the edge of the sword and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok (Num 21:23–24). The victory at Jahaz opened the whole country of Sihon to the tribes of Reuben and Gad, and the town itself fell within the inheritance of Reuben (Josh 13:18). It was afterward given with its suburbs to the Levites of the family of Merari (Josh 21:36). In later ages, when Moab held the land, the prophets named Jahaz in their burdens against Moab, for its cry was heard in the day of that nation’s calamity (Isa 15:4; Jer 48:34). Jahaz thus marks the first great conquest east of Jordan, the opening blow by which the LORD began to give His people the land of the Amorite. It witnesses that when the enemies of God’s people refuse them peace and come out to battle, the LORD delivers the proud into the hands of His own.

Webster 1828 Definition

A town on the eastern tableland where Sihon the Amorite fought Israel and was overthrown.

expand to see more

JAHAZ, a town on the tableland east of the Jordan.

There Sihon the Amorite came out and fought against Israel (Num 21:23).

Israel smote him and possessed his land from Arnon to Jabbok (Num 21:24).

The town fell within the inheritance of Reuben (Josh 13:18).

It was given with its suburbs to the Levites of Merari (Josh 21:36).

Key Scripture

Num 21:23 — "And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel."

Num 21:24 — "And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong."

Josh 13:18 — "And Jahazah, and Kedemoth, and Mephaath,"

Josh 21:36 — "And out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer with her suburbs, and Jahazah with her suburbs,"

Modern Corruption

A place-name, not a doctrine in dispute; its lesson is that the LORD delivers the proud who refuse His people peace.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the overthrow of Sihon at Jahaz. Israel sought to pass in peace, but Sihon hardened his heart and came out to war; and the LORD delivered him into Israel’s hand. The proud who set themselves against the people of God, refusing every offer of peace, are broken; the battle they choose becomes their ruin.

Jahaz, the first great victory east of Jordan, also displays the faithfulness of God in beginning to give His people the land of promise. What He had sworn to Abraham He performed, town by town and battle by battle. The conquest was no accident of war but the unfolding of an ancient covenant, and Jahaz was its opening blow on the eastern side.

Hebrew Roots

The name is read as “a place trodden down” or “a battlefield,” fitting the scene of Sihon’s defeat.

expand to see more

Jahaz — Hebrew Yahats, perhaps “a place trodden down.”

It is also spelled Jahazah in the lists of towns.

It lay on the tableland of the Amorite kingdom.

It fell to Reuben and was given to the Merarite Levites.

The battlefield-town marked the opening conquest east of Jordan.

Usage

"Like Sihon at Jahaz, the proud who refuse God’s people peace are broken in the battle they choose."

"Jahaz teaches that the conquest unfolded an ancient covenant, town by town."

"The first victory east of Jordan witnesses the faithfulness of God to His promise to Abraham."
